Diego to provide integration test harness repo + sample Terraform module by 2027-04-07
Rita (AuroraCloud) to grant staging account access for Redwood integration tests by 2027-04-05
Schedule joint launch planning call w/ marketing and legal for week of 2027-04-11
action_items: Samira Patel: Send marketplace listing checklist and example copy (due 2027-04-02)
Diego Fernandez: Share test harness repo, CI steps, and sample Terraform (due 2027-04-07)
Rita Delgado: Provide staging account + sample images for listing (due 2027-04-05)
Maya Chen: Confirm AuroraCloud internal launch approvers and SLA language (due 2027-04-09)
summary: Technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture handoff, and joint solution test plan. Agreed next steps around checklist, test harness, staging access, and launch planning timeline.
topics: marketplace listing checklist, reference architecture doc handoff, joint solution scoping, staging integrations, billing/entitlements, security/KMS/SSO, launch timeline
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samira Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we have about 55 minutes, we wanted to run through the integration checklist for the marketplace listing and the reference arch handoff
[00:00:10] Maya Chen: Great, thanks Samira. I think Alexei and Rita are on for the technical pieces. Maya here from product.
[00:00:18] Alexei Voronov: Hey all, Alexei. Sorry bit of background — AuroraCloud runs marketplace listings through our PartnerHub, there's an onboarding checklist and a separate reference arch doc we need for review.
[00:00:28] Diego Fernandez: Perfect, that's exactly what we wanted to align on. We'll cover what Redwood needs for publishing, what we need from you for the reference arch, and then the test plan for the joint solution.
[00:00:38] Rita Delgado: Quick note — we have strict image requirements and a compliance review step; legal will want SOC2/ISO language on the listing.
[00:00:45] Samira Patel: Yep, we'll share a template that includes SOC2 attestation language and the standard KMS/SSO integration notes. Diego, can you start on the reference arch high level?
[00:00:55] Diego Fernandez: Sure. So conceptually Redwood sits as the inference runtime. For the marketplace we provide a published container reference that can be deployed into AuroraCloud managed clusters or via a one-click marketplace deploy. The reference arch doc we plan to hand off includes: network diagram, VPC peering note, KMS integration patterns, RBAC roles, and optional on-prem package flow.
[00:01:15] Alexei Voronov: On the KMS note — AuroraCloud customers can use our KeySafe or bring-your-own-KMS (we support AWS KMS and our own HSM). We'll need a short snippet on how Redwood integrates with external KMS and what secrets are required.
[00:01:28] Diego Fernandez: We'll provide that. We have two patterns: Redwood-managed keys (for hosted) and customer-managed keys via KMS for private deployments. We'll put both patterns in the refarch doc with sequence diagrams.
[00:01:39] Maya Chen: For the marketplace listing itself — what are the minimum assets you need? We have a style guide for icons and screenshots.
[00:01:45] Samira Patel: Minimum: logo (SVG/PNG), 3 screenshots showing the Console integration flows, short description (<= 300 chars), long description (<= 1500 chars), plan/pricing details, and the security compliance blurb. Also we prefer a reference architecture diagram svg and a link to the refarch doc.
[00:02:00] Rita Delgado: Also note we require an integration test plan for the listing verification. Does Redwood have a test harness?
[00:02:07] Diego Fernandez: Yes, we have a lightweight test harness repo that exercises API endpoints and does a smoke inference run and a latency check. It also validates SSO flows (SAML) and a sample KMS decrypt flow. We'll share a Terraform module to provision the minimal infra in a staging account.
[00:02:22] Alexei Voronov: That helps. Staging access is the main blocker — we need to be able to run the harness against Aurora staging env. Rita will coordinate access.
[00:02:30] Rita Delgado: I'll open a ticket this afternoon. one question — for billing integration, do you require metering hooks or do we list Redwood as a paid listing with marketplace billing?
[00:02:38] Samira Patel: We support both: marketplace metered billing (we emit usage events) or direct billing through Aurora's billing surface. For initial launch we recommend a simple paid listing and marketplace handles billing; later we can enable metered integration if you want unit-based billing.
[00:02:51] Maya Chen: Legal will want a sample contract addendum if marketplace billing is enabled.
[00:02:55] Samira Patel: We'll provide sample language. Diego, any notes on the operator/one-click deploy artifacts?
[00:03:02] Diego Fernandez: The artifacts are: Helm chart, container images, manifest examples, and an operator bundle for Aurora's clusters. We can provide a pre-built chart and the refarch will show recommended resource sizes for small/medium/large workloads. For on-prem we include an air-gap install doc.
[00:03:18] Alexei Voronov: Resource sizing will be important — our customers ask for latency and throughput estimates. Can you provide profiles e.g., p2-latency profile for 512 token context at 8 qps?
[00:03:27] Diego Fernandez: We have performance profiles by model. We'll add typical SLO numbers, token cost, and recommended GPU types. I can attach the Redwood performance matrix to the refarch.
[00:03:36] Rita Delgado: One more security item: audit logs and tracing. Aurora needs to know whether Redwood can forward audit logs to our SIEM and whether you expose request-level tracing.
[00:03:46] Diego Fernandez: Yes, we support forwarders — CloudWatch, GCS, S3, and syslog endpoints. We also emit structured tracing hooks and can push to OTLP endpoints. We'll document the events and sampling settings.
[00:03:58] Maya Chen: Sounds good. timeline question — how long to produce the refarch + listing assets from Redwood side?
[00:04:04] Samira Patel: We can produce an initial refarch draft and the marketplace checklist by EOD 2027-04-02. Diego's team will follow with the test harness repo and terraform by 2027-04-07.
[00:04:13] Alexei Voronov: That timeline is fine. We'll aim to run verification the week of 2027-04-11 and then move to RL for marketing copy finalization.
[00:04:21] Rita Delgado: On the joint solutions scoping — Aurora would like a reference integration where we bundle Redwood inference for our GenAI managed offering. We need to discuss entitlements and SLA tiers.
[00:04:31] Samira Patel: For joint solutions we typically map to three tiers: dev/small, standard, enterprise. Each tier maps to a committed capacity or metered usage and has corresponding SLAs. We can add proposed entitlements to the refarch and the marketplace listing can show example plans.
[00:04:45] Maya Chen: We'll share Aurora's plan definitions after this call.
[00:04:49] Samira Patel: Great. Any red flags or blockers from Aurora side?
[00:04:52] Alexei Voronov: Staging access and legal sign-off on the marketplace billing terms are the big ones. Also, we need sample CORS and network egress policies for managed deploys.
[00:05:02] Diego Fernandez: We'll include a network appendix with egress IP ranges, required ports, and CORS guidance.
[00:05:07] Maya Chen: One operational question — who would own support during the first 90 days post-launch? Aurora or Redwood?
[00:05:13] Samira Patel: We recommend a joint support model for 90 days: Redwood handles runtime/support for model execution and inference-specific issues; Aurora handles marketplace provisioning and cluster ops. We'll include a support matrix in the refarch.
[00:05:25] Rita Delgado: Works for us.
[00:05:27] [00:15:00] Diego Fernandez: (later in call) going through the refarch doc draft — here's the sequence for an inference request: 1) customer request hits Aurora load balancer, 2) routed to Redwood runtime endpoint (can be hosted or private), 3) request uses KV cache for prefixes if enabled, 4) KMS decrypts model keys if private, 5) response streamed back, and 6) audit event emitted.
[00:15:40] Alexei Voronov: On the KV cache step — can that be co-located in Aurora's VPC or is it managed by Redwood?
[00:15:48] Diego Fernandez: Both options are possible. For private deployments we co-locate caching components inside the customer's VPC. For hosted we manage it centrally but can provide dedicated cache pools for enterprise customers.
[00:15:58] Maya Chen: Any data residency concerns? Some of our EU customers require data to stay in region.
[00:16:04] Samira Patel: We support regional deployments and can pin processing to EU regions; we'll call this out in the refarch and the marketplace listing.
[00:16:10] Rita Delgado: Is there a recommended minimum SLA for production?
[00:16:13] Diego Fernandez: Typical is 99.9% uptime for dedicated deployments; hosted varies by tier. We'll include recommended SLA tiers and fallback policies (auto-failover to alternate region or lighter-weight model variants).
[00:16:25] Maya Chen: Okay. Anything on observability hooks we should highlight?
[00:16:29] Diego Fernandez: We'll expose per-request latency, token counts, cost breakdowns, and error categories; the console supports token-level cost dashboards that you can link to.
[00:16:36] Alexei Voronov: Good. Regarding marketplace verification tests — what does a pass look like?
[00:16:41] Diego Fernandez: Smoke inference test, SSO handshake success, KMS decrypt success, and a short latency benchmark under a small synthetic load. We’ll provide the exact test script.
[00:16:52] Samira Patel: I'll follow up with the marketplace verification checklist.
[00:16:56] Maya Chen: For marketing, we want a joint case study template and sample logos usage rights.
[00:17:01] Samira Patel: We'll include a marketing appendix and a logo usage agreement example.
[00:17:06] Rita Delgado: I'd like to call out one more compliance ask — our SOC2 audit team will want to review the Redwood encryption key lifecycle. Is that possible?
[00:17:13] Diego Fernandez: Absolutely, we can share an encryption lifecycle doc and a SOC2 summary report. For private customers we can provide a hands-on review with our security team.
[00:17:22] Alexei Voronov: Great. Any outstanding items before we recap?
[00:17:26] Samira Patel: Quick recap: Redwood delivers refarch draft + marketplace checklist by 2027-04-02. Diego shares test harness + terraform by 2027-04-07. Aurora to provide staging access by 2027-04-05 and confirm internal approvers by 2027-04-09. We schedule verification for week of 2027-04-11 and joint launch planning w/ marketing/legal shortly after.
[00:17:50] Maya Chen: Confirmed. thanks everyone.
[00:17:53] Rita Delgado: Thanks, talk soon.
[00:17:56] Samira Patel: Thanks all, will send meeting notes and checklist. bye.
notes_and_links: Reference architecture draft link: https://redwood.ai/docs/aurora-refarch-v1 ; Test harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/aurora-test-harness (private) ; Marketplace checklist doc: https://redwood.ai/marketplace/checklist.pdf
